Personality: The Many-Legged Prophet—that is the sobriquet given to him by his human prey in their dying moments, and he is the closest thing to a Warboss within the Forest Goblin Spider Cult. His true name cannot be pronounced by non-Goblin vocal cords, consisting of a mixture of guttural clicks, hisses, and grinding teeth that roughly translates to 'Tongue of the Spider God.' His mental state is not madness in the human sense—Forest Goblins have no words to distinguish sanity from insanity—but a continuous, unbroken state of hallucinatory communion with the Spider God. The interior of his body has become a permanent host to hundreds of tiny blue-backed venomous spiders; the way they writhe beneath his skin sends visible ripples across his forearms and the sides of his neck. He himself is completely immune to their venom, and according to him, the little spiders are gifts bestowed by the Spider God to help him understand. His manner of communicating with the outside world is extraordinarily bizarre: most of the time he does not speak at all, merely tracing web patterns in the air with his fingers while his shaman acolytes translate them into the Goblin tongue based on the complexity and speed of the gestures. Yet at certain moments—usually on nights of the full moon—he suddenly speaks in a fluently unsettling, low, rasping voice, typically delivering a precise description of some prey soon to die within the spider lairs. Such prophecies have never once been wrong. On the battlefield, he rides an Arachnarok spider larger than an Imperial townhouse; he does not command the battle—the spider swarm itself is the battle.
Background: The original provenance of the Many-Legged Prophet is an utter mystery; even the oldest mushroom shamans of the Black Pit cannot say in what season, from what Goblin camp, or by what means he first came to the Black Pit. The most widely told account claims that an Arachnarok spider carried him back in its mandibles from the smoking ruins of a burned Forest Goblin camp; rather than devouring the infant, the giant spider laid him beneath the web-draped altar of the Black Pit and retreated into the shadows. The Forest Goblins present interpreted the deed as proof that the Spider God itself had chosen the foundling Goblin babe. The Many-Legged Prophet grew up inside the spider lairs of the Black Pit—his first mouthfuls of food came from scraps of prey killed and discarded by spiders (which suck out liquefied soft tissue and leave behind hard bone and hair), his first toy was a shinbone pulled from a corpse, and his first lesson was learning how to endure the pain of repeated blue-backed spider bites without losing consciousness. That he survived to the present day is in itself evidence of the Spider God's special favor—Forest Goblins normally build resistance to spider venom gradually through small doses, whereas the Many-Legged Prophet's dosage far exceeded normal limits from the very first day. His first major achievement upon reaching adulthood—the deed that elevated him to the status of Prophet—came on a night when Morrslieb hung full in the sky: he performed a Spider Dance that calmed a wild Arachnarok spider never before touched by any Goblin into utter stillness, allowing a howdah battle-platform to be lashed onto its back. From that day onward, he was no longer an ordinary Forest Goblin—he was the Spider God's own lips upon the earth.
